text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- From January 1997 Portugal's public television channel RTP1 can only have seven and a half minutes of publicity per hour while private televisions TVI and SIC accepted a 12-minute limit. Advertisers are not happy.
- Right-wing Popular Party (PP) leader Manuel Monteiro's popularity has fallen again. Monteiro is behind Communist Party leader Carlos Carvalhas, says an opinion poll.
- Government prepared to make changes in Lisbon's Expo-98 World exhibition if the information it is collecting shows mismanagement.
- The government decision on television advertising will cost the state channels five billion escudos ($32 million).
- Portuguese economic growth may exceed three percent in 1998, according to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
